method: Thirty-three State-recipient-specific passes. A pass may verify mission fit, correct routing, narrow a claim, preserve a falsifier, separate an evidence class, or improve diplomatic actionability. Mere compatibility with the hypothesis is not a pass.

passes.finding: The issue is framed as foreign-policy and partner-resilience risk: open-information reach, international communications policy, digital freedom, cyber policy and diplomatic early warning.
Current State FAM organization codes, updated 2026-08-18, list the Bureau of Cyberspace and Digital Policy and its ICP, ICS and Digital Freedom components.
1 FAM assigns Digital Freedom responsibility for digital information integrity and defending against repressive state-controlled practices in cyberspace.
CDP/ICP is responsible for international communications and information policy and liaison with foreign governments and interagency partners.
CDP/ICS fits diplomatic cyber-security, partner capacity and adversary-related cyberspace policy, while the letter avoids asking State to perform operational network exploitation.

Current 2026 organization codes identify the Bureau of Emerging Threats with an Office of Threat Assessment and Office of Cybersecurity. State v4 requests routing there as a secondary cross-domain destination.
INR/CET is current and has an explicit mission to analyze foreign-government cyber, telecommunications and emerging-technology issues; it is included as an internal analytic destination.

State administrative codes still list R/CFIMI, but 2026 public court filings state the Hub had been ordered closed in 2025. v4 treats the status as publicly inconsistent and does not rely on R/CFIMI as the live intake endpoint.
v4 asks State to route to any current component retaining foreign-information-manipulation responsibilities rather than assuming a specific successor office.
JUXTAPOSE is absent. FBI-only rule preserved.
State v4 is not an ODNI duplicate: center of gravity is partner resilience, open information access, source diversity, diplomatic baselines and international technology policy.
The letter notes that the counterintelligence-specific lead was already submitted to FBI and does not ask State to duplicate investigation/enforcement.
The platform-specific seed-to-organic lead is described as already sent to Meta; State receives only the partner-resilience implications.
The integrated intelligence collection-gap version was already sent to ODNI/NCSC; State v4 asks a diplomatic resilience question instead.
Crimea, Donbas and occupied-Ukraine distribution/source control remain high-confidence mechanism precedents; Georgia, Syria and Chechnya controls prevent a universal doctrine claim.
TSPU is described as domestic, centrally controlled and in-path with protocol-selective behavior; no foreign-node claim is inferred.
Mobile deny-except-allowlist capability is preserved as a source-isolation mechanism while fixed, satellite and dedicated paths remain outside the claim.
Russian-side border-crossing control is distinguished from foreign TSPU deployment or arbitrary foreign-origin censorship.
SORM, commercial DPI, lawful intercept and TSPU remain analytically distinct throughout the letter.
Russian-origin telecom surveillance/DPI exports are framed as a partner supply-chain and control-plane collection surface, not evidence of Russian command.
Vendor support access, software update authority and state remote control are separated. The proposed test asks what privileges actually exist.
DOJ/FBI and Meta precedents establish fake-persona/bot/audience-seeding tactic classes without attributing current Threads activity.
The current Threads wave is a secondary platform-resilience example rather than the subject of the State submission.
Profile presentation is not treated as verified age; minors, targeting and operator identity remain NOT_ESTABLISHED.
Early-linked/late-independent is retained as the key seed-to-organic discriminator; fully independent cohorts weaken/reject the concern.
v4 emphasizes foreign reachability loss while U.S. services remain healthy, local substitutes survive, source diversity falls, and relative narrative exposure may change.
The letter says degraded/delayed observability, not American blindness, and explicitly names alternate diplomatic, civil-society, provider and intelligence observation channels.
Technical blame-shifting is included only with mandatory controls for sanctions, Western geoblocking, real provider failures, cache degradation and platform policy.
Phrase similarity, old account age and old media are not attribution evidence alone; chronology, context substitution and independent operator evidence are required.
The submission explicitly avoids requesting policing of lawful political views and focuses on hidden coordination, network access and state-controlled distribution mechanisms.

Ten defensive partner-baseline indicators are provided: paired vantages, access-layer separation, path evidence, vendor control-plane inventory, country baselines, substitute-source monitoring, platform integrity liaison, narrative timing, embassy/civil-society reporting and falsification-first review.
Independent policy timing, ordinary outages, local sovereign control, authentic users, commercial SMM and absence of path-localized filtering count against the hypothesis.

v4 is recipient-specific, bounded, falsifiable, references the complete public evidence branch, discloses prior scoped submissions, and contains no JUXTAPOSE. User has explicitly authorized sending after completion of the presend work.

material_changes_from_v3: Reframed recipient from CDP+CFIMI to current State routing centered on CDP, Emerging Threats and INR/CET, with foreign-information-manipulation successor routing requested as appropriate.
Added explicit public-record conflict concerning R/CFIMI status rather than falsely treating it as certainly active.
Added current 2026 Bureau of Emerging Threats / Office of Threat Assessment and Office of Cybersecurity as relevant routing surfaces.
Added INR/CET as a current all-source analytic destination for foreign cyber/telecommunications questions.
Expanded State-specific partner-resilience baseline and diplomatic actionability.
Reduced the prominence of the current Threads case and made it a mechanism example rather than the central allegation.
Added Russian-side cross-border scope with explicit foreign-node ceiling.
Strengthened free-expression safeguard language and explicit non-enforcement framing.
Preserved technical blame shifting, phrase lineage, account repurposing and old-media context substitution as secondary indicators only.
Preserved all principal falsifiers and negative controls.

routing_assessment.electronic_public_route: Use publicly listed State/CDP contact addresses and request internal routing; do not invent a CFIMI mailbox.
